items.followUp: State two differences between star topology and ring topology.

rubric.why: Identifies the shared central cable and how devices attach to it.
rubric.description: Bus topology uses one main backbone cable to which devices are connected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the common backbone and device connections.

rubric.why: Identifies the direct links between devices in a mesh.
rubric.description: In a full mesh, each device has a dedicated link to every other device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the dedicated device-to-device connections.

rubric.why: Shows the effect of failure of the bus's shared cable.
rubric.description: Failure of the bus backbone can bring down the whole network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct failure effect.

rubric.why: States a key advantage of mesh topology resulting from its multiple links.
rubric.description: Mesh topology is highly reliable and fault tolerant because alternative links may remain available.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid reliability or fault-tolerance comparison.

modelAnswer: Bus topology: all devices are connected to one common backbone cable.
Mesh topology: each device is connected to every other device by a dedicated link (in a full mesh).
In bus topology, failure of the backbone can stop communication across the whole network.
Mesh topology is highly reliable and fault tolerant because other links can continue working if one link fails.

items.followUp: Give four privacy risks that can result from collecting large amounts of personal data.

rubric.why: Gives an example of collection that disregards the person's permission.
rubric.description: Personal data may be collected without a person's consent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying collection without consent or permission.

rubric.why: Gives an example of data being shared or used beyond its original purpose.
rubric.description: Collected data may be sold or shared with third parties without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sale or unauthorized sharing of data.

rubric.why: Identifies harm that can occur when personal information is misused.
rubric.description: Personal information may be misused for identity theft or fraud.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identity theft, fraud, or a similarly specific misuse.

rubric.why: Identifies exposure of stored personal data as a privacy risk.
rubric.description: A security breach or data leak can expose private information to unauthorized people.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a data breach, leak, or unauthorized access.

modelAnswer: Personal data may be collected without a person's consent.
Collected data may be sold or shared with third parties without permission.
Personal information may be misused for identity theft or fraud.
A security breach or data leak may expose private information to unauthorized people.

items.followUp: What is meant by Invalid Test Data?

rubric.why: Defines valid data by its expected type, range, or format.
rubric.description: Valid test data has the correct type and format and falls within the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data meets the program's requirements.

rubric.why: Explains why valid test data is used.
rubric.description: It is used to check that a program processes acceptable input and produces the expected output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its testing purpose.

modelAnswer: Valid test data is input that has the correct type and format and lies within the acceptable range for a program.
It is used to check whether the program processes acceptable input and produces the expected output.

items.followUp: Name four types of secondary storage device.

rubric.why: Recognizes two valid examples of storage devices.
rubric.description: Names two storage devices, such as a hard disk and an optical disc.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

rubric.why: Recognizes two further valid examples of storage devices.
rubric.description: Names two further storage devices, such as a USB flash drive and a memory card.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two additional correct examples; accept other valid storage devices.

modelAnswer: Examples of storage devices are: hard disk, optical disc, USB flash drive, and memory card.

rubric.why: Shows the place-value expansion of the binary number.
rubric.description: Expands the binary digits using powers of 2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct place-value expansion, such as 1×2^6 + 1×2^0.

rubric.why: Gives the correct decimal value.
rubric.description: Converts (1000001)₂ to 65₁₀.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct decimal answer.

items.followUp: State two differences between RAM and a hard disk.

rubric.why: Describes the temporary nature of main memory.
rubric.description: Memory (such as RAM) holds data temporarily and is usually volatile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory is temporary or volatile.

rubric.why: Contrasts storage with temporary memory.
rubric.description: Storage keeps data for long-term use and is generally non-volatile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that storage retains data long-term or without power.

modelAnswer: Memory (such as RAM) temporarily holds data and instructions that the computer is currently using; it is usually volatile.
Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use and is generally non-volatile.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: Checks that both input cases for the NOT operator are shown.
rubric.description: Includes the input values 0 and 1 for A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing both input cases in a truth table.

rubric.why: Checks that each input has the correct inverted output.
rubric.description: Shows the NOT output as 1 when A is 0, and 0 when A is 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct output values.

items.followUp: State the complement laws of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: Identifies the identity law for OR.
rubric.description: The identity law for OR is A + 0 = A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct OR identity law.

rubric.why: Identifies the identity law for AND.
rubric.description: The identity law for AND is A · 1 = A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct AND identity law.

modelAnswer: The identity law for OR is A + 0 = A.
The identity law for AND is A · 1 = A.
